title: Renting a Flat
description: Four recordings about renting a flat: a phone call to an agent, a flat viewing, a landlord voicemail and a podcast with advice.
instructions: Read the questions for each part first. Then press Play and listen. Choose the best answer for each question.

parts.title: Part 1 · A call to an agent
parts.intro: You will hear Nam phoning an estate agent, Ms Taylor, about flats to rent.

script.speaker: Ms Taylor
script.text: Good morning, Parkside Lettings. Ms Taylor speaking.

script.speaker: Nam
script.text: Hello. I'm calling about the two-bedroom flat on Orchard Road that you advertised online.

script.speaker: Ms Taylor
script.text: Yes, it's still available. It's on the second floor, and the rent is nine hundred and fifty pounds a month.

script.speaker: Nam
script.text: That's a bit more than I expected. Does that include bills?

script.speaker: Ms Taylor
script.text: Water is included, but you pay for electricity and internet yourself. The deposit is one month's rent.

script.speaker: Nam
script.text: I see. And is it furnished?

script.speaker: Ms Taylor
script.text: Partly. There's a bed in each room, a sofa and a fridge, but no washing machine. The landlord says you can bring your own.

script.speaker: Nam
script.text: Are pets allowed? I have a small cat.

script.speaker: Ms Taylor
script.text: Sorry, not in this building. But there's another flat on Mill Street, a bit smaller, where cats are fine. It's eight hundred and fifty pounds.

script.speaker: Nam
script.text: Hmm, I'd like to see both, if possible.

script.speaker: Ms Taylor
script.text: Certainly. I can show you Orchard Road on Thursday at five, and Mill Street on Friday morning at ten. Could I take your phone number?

parts.title: Part 2 · Viewing the flat
parts.intro: You will hear a landlord, Mr Wood, showing a flat to Mai.

script.speaker: Mai
script.text: Hello, Mr Wood. Thank you for showing me the flat.

script.speaker: Mr Wood
script.text: My pleasure. Come in. As you can see, the living room gets lots of light in the morning because the windows face east.

script.speaker: Mai
script.text: It's lovely. And the kitchen?

script.speaker: Mr Wood
script.text: It was repainted last month. The cooker is new, but the oven door is a little stiff, so I'll ask someone to fix it before you move in.

script.speaker: Mai
script.text: Good. What about the bedrooms?

script.speaker: Mr Wood
script.text: The big one overlooks the garden, which is very quiet. The smaller one is next to the road, so you'll hear traffic, I'm afraid.

script.speaker: Mai
script.text: I could use that one as an office. I work from home two days a week.

script.speaker: Mr Wood
script.text: That would be perfect. And the internet is fast here, so there shouldn't be any problems.

script.speaker: Mai
script.text: What are the neighbours like?

script.speaker: Mr Wood
script.text: Very friendly. An older couple live downstairs, and they've been here for thirty years. The only rule is no loud music after ten o'clock.

script.speaker: Mai
script.text: That's fine with me. I'd like to take it. When could I move in?

script.speaker: Mr Wood
script.text: On the first of next month. I'll send the contract tomorrow.

parts.title: Part 3 · A message from the landlord
parts.intro: You will hear a voicemail message from a landlord, Mr Khan, to his tenant.

script.speaker: Mr Khan
script.text: Hello, this is Mr Khan, your landlord. I'm calling about the leak in your bathroom that you reported last week.

script.speaker: Mr Khan
script.text: I'm sorry it took so long. A plumber is coming on Wednesday between nine and twelve. Someone needs to be home to let him in, so if you're at work, you can leave a key with Mrs Perez next door.

script.speaker: Mr Khan
script.text: The job should take about two hours. You'll have no water for part of that time, so please fill a few bottles in advance.

script.speaker: Mr Khan
script.text: Also, I'd like to remind you that the rent is due on the fifth of each month. This month's payment hasn't arrived yet. I'm sure it's a mistake, but please check your bank account.

script.speaker: Mr Khan
script.text: One more thing. The building's front door lock is being changed on Friday, and you'll receive a new key at the office. Please collect it before six o'clock, because the office closes then.

script.speaker: Mr Khan
script.text: Call me on my mobile if you have any questions. Thanks very much. Goodbye.

parts.title: Part 4 · Tips for first-time renters
parts.intro: You will hear Hannah on a podcast for students.

script.speaker: Hannah
script.text: Hi, everyone, and welcome to Student Life. Today I'm sharing advice for anyone renting a flat for the first time.

script.speaker: Hannah
script.text: First, read the contract carefully. It may be boring, but it explains how long you must stay and how much notice you must give before leaving. Many students sign without reading, and they get a nasty surprise later.

script.speaker: Hannah
script.text: Second, take photographs of everything on the day you move in, especially any marks on the walls or floor. If you don't, the landlord might say you caused the damage, and you could lose part of your deposit.

script.speaker: Hannah
script.text: Third, think about the total cost, not only the rent. Bills, internet and transport can add another two hundred pounds a month. A cheap flat far from the city centre isn't always cheaper.

script.speaker: Hannah
script.text: Finally, if you share with friends, agree on the rules from the start. Who cleans the bathroom? Who pays for what? Honestly, most arguments I've seen weren't about money, but about dirty dishes.

script.speaker: Hannah
script.text: Renting can be a wonderful first step towards independence. Just be prepared, and you'll enjoy it.
